content.title: Tennyson Street Bike Lane & Sidewalk Improvements
content.summary: The City is enhancing pedestrian and cyclist safety along Tennyson Street from 64th to 58th avenues by improving sidewalks, adding bike lanes, and upgrading crossings, including a new crosswalk with a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon. This project, which is grant-funded and coordinated with a separate sewer line replacement, aims to better connect local schools, parks, and transit stops, with construction expected to last 3 to 4 months once it begins. Residents may experience temporary disruptions, including limited driveway access and construction noise.
content.body:
## Overview

The City is improving the connectivity and safety for pedestrians and cyclists from 64th to 58th avenues along Tennyson Street. The project will include:

- Improved sidewalk from 60th to 62nd avenues on the west side of Tennyson
- Bike lanes from 58th to 64th avenues
- Improved crossing at 60th and Tennyson, including a crosswalk with a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB)
- Stormwater system improvements along the corridor

This project will improve connected routes to local assets including neighborhood schools, parks, and transit stops.

**Please note:**A [sewer line replacement project](/1030) is also being planned along Tennyson to replace aging infrastructure and improve capacity. Both projects are being coordinated by the City of Arvada. However, they will have separate timelines and potential impacts along the corridor.

Both projects will provide improvements to the community. Thank you for your patience and understanding during the construction.

![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=3758)

## Timeline

Update 7/28/25: the project team continues to coordinate permits and design approval.

Once work begins, the project is expected to take approximately 3 to 4 months.

The project is grant funded in partnership with Adams County. The project requires coordination and approval from the county. Construction timeline is still being determined. Please check back for timeline updates.

## What to Expect

- Working hours: 7 am - 7 pm
  - Work will be limited during school arrival and dismissal (7:00-8:00 am and 2:30-3:30 pm)
- Construction traffic and noise may be present
- Occasional single lane closures
  - Alternating one-way traffic with flaggers as needed
- Driveway access may be limited to some properties along Tennyson
  - Impacted residents will be notified for coordination

### [FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=83)

[Will there be impacts to my property?](#)
:   Residents with driveways on Tennyson may have limited impacts to their property. These residents will be notified directly for coordination.

[Will there be conflicts between the sewer line and roadway projects in this area?](#)
:   While the [sewer line](/1030) and [roadway](/1031) projects are on separate timelines, there is a chance for some overlap in work. If any overlap occurs, the projects will coordinate impacts and inform the community as necessary.

[Is there work planned along 60th Avenue?](#)
:   No. All work for both the roadway and sewer line projects will take place on Tennyson Street. There will be work at the intersection of Tennyson and 60th for both projects to install the crosswalk features.

    Tennyson was identified as a higher priority, and received grant funding from Adams County, for bike lane and sidewalk improvements due to connectivity to surrounding public amenities including schools, parks, trails, and public transit. The 60th Avenue corridor is on the City’s radar for future improvements. The City is looking for grant funding opportunities, including a safety study currently in progress by Adams County.

    For more information on the City’s planning for connecting bike / pedestrian routes visit the City’s [2017 bicycle master plan](https://www.arvadaco.gov/DocumentCenter/View/778/2017-Bicycle-Master-Plan-PDF).

/FAQ.aspx

## Contact

Please submit questions or concerns to [Ask Arvada](/898). A team member will be in touch.
